script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

CAROLINE (mid 30s, wearing glasses, messy hair) sits alone at a table, surrounded by laptop-wielding twenty-somethings. She stirs her coffee absentmindedly, staring at the page in front of her.

WAITRESS (mid 20s) approaches, setting down a fresh cup of coffee.

WAITRESS
(cheerful)
You look like you could use another cup. And it looks like you could use a break.

Caroline smiles wanly.

CAROLINE
I've been writing the same sentence for three hours now.

WAITRESS
(sympathetic)
Oh no. What's the project?

CAROLINE
A novel about second chances.

WAITRESS
(nods)
Ah, those can be tough to write. Maybe you need a second chance yourself.

Caroline looks up, surprised.

CAROLINE
What do you mean?

WAITRESS
Why don't you join us for lunch? My friends and I are having a potluck. I bet you could use a change of scenery.

INT. WAITRESS'S APARTMENT - LIVING ROOM - LATER

Caroline sits on a plush sofa, surrounded by colorful plates of food. A group of friends chats and laughs, including the WAITRESS, JASMINE (late 20s, wearing a vibrant dress), and LUCAS (early 30s, with a beard and glasses).

JASMINE
(to Caroline)
So, what's your story? Why do you write about second chances?

CAROLINE
(hesitant)
I've made some mistakes in my past. And I've missed some opportunities. I guess I'm trying to explore what it would be like to have another chance.

LUCAS
(supportive)
We all make mistakes, Caroline. And sometimes, we get a second chance. Like when I accidentally texted my ex-girlfriend instead of my current girlfriend.

Everyone groans.

WAITRESS
(laughing)
But you managed to salvage things, right?

LUCAS
(smiling)
Yes, I did.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY - A WEEK LATER

Caroline sits at her usual table, laptop open in front of her. She looks up as the WAITRESS approaches, carrying a tray of pastries.

WAITRESS
(smiling)
You're back to your coffee again. How's the novel coming?

CAROLINE
(smiling back)
It's coming along. I had an idea last night.

WAITRESS
(excited)
Really? Tell me!

CAROLINE
(confident)
It's about a woman who gets a second chance at love, but she has to face her fears and overcome her past. And she does it with the help of some unlikely friends.

WAITRESS
(impressed)
Wow, that sounds great! I can't wait to read it.

INT. LUCAS'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Caroline sits on the couch, surrounded by piles of manuscript pages. Lucas sits next to her, reading over her shoulder.

LUCAS
(encouraging)
You've got a real knack for this, Caroline.

CAROLINE
(nervous)
I don't know, Lucas. What if it's not good enough?

LUCAS
(reassuring)
It will be. And if it's not, we'll figure something out. But for now, let's focus on the positive.

INT. LIBRARY - DAY - A MONTH LATER

Caroline sits at a table, surrounded by books. She looks up as JASMINE approaches, wearing a librarian's uniform.

JASMINE
(excited)
Caroline! I got a job here! And I thought you could use a hand.

Caroline grins.

CAROLINE
I'd love to help out. And it's a second chance for me, too. A chance to give back to the community.

JASMINE
(smiling)
Perfect. Let's get to work.

FADE OUT.

THE END
